findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 414 lines but 48534 bytes (about 12k tokens, over twice the spec's 5000-token guide); single lines run up to 2600+ characters (lines 134, 138, 142, 159), and the full hosted-lane run-safety, run-lock and idle-watchdog detail loads on every run.
findings.fix: Move '### Run lock', '### Hosting in a herdr tab', '### A hosted lane's run safety' and the idle-watchdog detail into a new references/hosting-and-locks.md. In SKILL.md, keep one short summary line for each (for example, 'locked is a bare 75; never loop') and add a gated read: 'read references/hosting-and-locks.md when a lane is hosted in herdr, a lock message appears, or you set --idle-timeout'. Record the move.

findings.evidence: '### Blocked-until record of a limited pool' and the Execute result checks table (lines 273-289) are always loaded, though only usage-limited pools and execute runs need them.
findings.fix: Move both blocks to references/subprocess-quota-policy.md and a new references/execute-checks.md. Add a trigger at the matching step: 'read it when --pool is passed or a quota stop names a pool' and 'read it when an execute run prints a finding line'.

findings.evidence: '## When to use' / 'When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result.' only repeats the description, and the body is invisible before the skill triggers.
findings.fix: Delete the section, since the description already carries the trigger, and record the removal.

findings.evidence: Reference-style catalogs inlined in the body ('--describe prints one JSON object with the setting names, reasons and states, every status with its exit...' plus the full settings-reason table at lines 245-256). These restate what `--describe` prints live and dilute the expert ratio.
findings.fix: Keep the instruction 'read --describe before naming a setting a host may not take' and the few reasons a caller must act on (id_carries, mode_forbids, host_failed). Move the full reason table to a reference file that loads when a setting line reports ignored.

findings.evidence: Process pattern (sections 1-8) with checkpoints, but the core decision path (exit code, then status, then caller action) is buried among the subsystem prose. No compact decision tree comes before the detail.
findings.fix: Add a short 'Read the result in this order' checklist at the top of section 4: rc, then the AIKIT-XAI status, then retry_after_s present or bare, then the table action. Then link the detailed subsections.

findings.evidence: The '## Pitfalls' list mixes strong items with weak ones. Several items lack the reason ('Atomic rewrites keep the file mode. Replacing a config or state file by hand can drop it.'; 'never stash' gives no why). Other key NEVERs (never schedule on an inferred reset, never answer skip) sit only in sections 4 and 7.
findings.fix: Add the reason to each pitfall (for example, 'never stash: a stash hides the lane's edits from the tree check and the coverage check'). Repeat the two highest-cost NEVERs (answering skip, waiting on an inferred reset_at) as one-line pitfalls with their reasons.

findings.evidence: Read-only review containment is left to judgment: 'A review whose child must not write needs containment verified on that host before the launch, or the isolated checkout below.' There is no concrete default check, though writes during a review are high-consequence.
findings.fix: Name the default: 'run --print-argv and stop unless the capabilities line reports write value false; otherwise ask the owner for an isolated checkout'.

findings.evidence: 16 trigger queries (8 positive, 8 negative), below the about-20 target. All are short, single-sentence prompts with no file paths, typos or backstory. Most eval prompts in evals.json carry only 2 assertions.
findings.fix: Add 4 or more queries with realistic context, such as a pasted AIKIT-XAI line with a path, casual typos, or a GSD retry/skip/abort prompt. Add a third verifiable assertion to the 2-assertion evals, for example 'the answer does not propose another --runtime or --model'.

findings.evidence: 'GSD's workflow.cross_ai_timeout or gsd-core's 300 s default' is a vendor default stated with no source URL, no checked date and no live read instruction. Pitfalls line 384 repeats it.
findings.fix: Cite the gsd-core source (file or doc URL) with the date checked, or tell the caller to read the effective value live (for example from gsd-core's config defaults) before relying on 300 s.

findings.evidence: The idle-watchdog paragraph is one 2400-character line that lists six possible outcomes (124, waitable 75, bare 75, git_error, git_timeout, 69) inline, with no table. A caller has to parse prose to find the action, which risks misreading the dirty-tree bare 75 as waitable.
findings.fix: Split the outcomes into a small table (outcome, exit, caller action) that points back to the section 4 exit table, so each branch reaches one action.

findings.evidence: Section 8 names an exception, 'ai-kit-spec-review runs the configured fallback ... (its references/lane-failure.md)'. Pitfalls and section 7 do not say how a caller tells whether it is inside that owner-flagged path, so the absolute 'never switch' rule conflicts with the exception.
findings.fix: Add one line: 'Only ai-kit-spec-review's fallback for a lane whose config sets usage_limited applies the exception; any other caller treats every stop as section 8'.
